title: `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()` does not respect `'splitright'`
body:
### Problem

With the option `splitright` set, new window should split to the right of the current window. `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()` opens on the left.

(nvim-treesitter/playground however works as expected and splits on the right)

### Steps to reproduce

I couldn't get treesitter to start with `nvim --clean`, but:

```
$ nvim +'h news'
:<nick> splitright
:<nick> vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()
```

### Expected behavior

Inspection tree opens on the right

### Neovim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.9.0-dev-1222+gf01f18cdf-dirty

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

-

### Operating system/version

macOS 13.2.1

### Terminal name/version

iTerm2 3.4.19

### $TERM environment variable

tmux-256color

### Installation

homebrew upgrade --fetch-HEAD neovim

comments.body: PR welcome

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
This is just a question about changing the default value of `command`
```
                • command (string|nil): Vimscript command to create the
                  window. Default value is "topleft 60vnew". Only used when
                  {winid} is nil.
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Yes, I thought about this as a fix:

```diff
diff --git a/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter.lua b/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter.lua
index 56000f99a..834757c4e 100644
--- a/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter.lua
+++ b/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter.lua
@@ -465,7 +465,11 @@ function M.inspect_tree(opts)

   local w = opts.winid
   if not w then
-    vim.cmd(opts.command or 'topleft 60vnew')
+    if vim.opt.splitright:get() then
+      vim.cmd(opts.command or 'botright 60vnew')
+    else
+      vim.cmd(opts.command or 'topleft 60vnew')
+    end
     w = a.nvim_get_current_win()
   end
```

Is that alright?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: We could also leave out the topleft/botright part. It's a better match with the file of which it is the syntax tree, but I get the desire to have a full-height syntax tree.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
No need to have separate, redundant `if` branches:

```lua
if not w then
  vim.cmd(opts.command or ('%s 60vnew'):<nick>(vim.o.splitright and 'botright' or 'topleft'))
end
```

>We could also leave out the topleft/botright part. It's a better match with the file of which it is the syntax tree, but I get the desire to have a full-height syntax tree.

The subjective nature of what is "better" is exactly why we have the ability to specify an arbitrary command. Unfortunately, we cannot satisfy everyone so we provide the user some flexibility.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: What's the rationale for using `topleft` by default?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> No need to have separate, redundant if branches:
>
> ```lua
> if not w then
>   vim.cmd(opts.command or ('%s 60vnew'):<nick>(vim.o.splitright and 'botright' or 'topleft'))
> end
> ```

Ah yes, forgot about using `and` and `or` like that.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> What's the rationale for using `topleft` by default?

Do you mean as opposed to `botright`? Arbitrary I suppose. IIRC the `nvim-treesitter/playground` plugin opens to the left too (at least it did when I used it), so I suppose I subconsciously modeled it after that.

If you mean why use `topleft` instead of just `vnew`, it is to have the window take up the full available height.

I'll grant that the default options were chosen for no other reason than "looks good to me". If there's a consensus on better defaults we can change.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> If you mean why use topleft instead of just vnew, it is to have the window take up the full available height.

Right I see. I think I feel pretty mixed about that. I think it's more predictable to just do `vnew`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> I think it's more predictable to just do vnew.

I agree.

Maybe introduce an option to `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()` to use the full height? Of course this is already possible using the `command` option, but I suspect not many users know the `topleft` and `botright` commands or other ways to do this.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant3 what do you think? I can make a PR removing the `topleft` part.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I am less concerned with `inspect_tree`, which is low-level and should arguably indeed not set any implicit defaults than with (the later addition) `:InspectTree`, which is now the main user interface.

If `inspect_tree` is changed, we shouldn't forget to adapt `InspectTree` accordingly.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Just a plain `:<nick>` is fine, or even `:<nick>`. Then user can do `:<nick> InspectTree` and similar. That is the standard vim idiom and avoids adding a bunch of options everywhere.



> Maybe introduce an option to `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()`

no

comments.body: +1 for `:<nick>`, as the output has a specific format that is indeed better suited to a vertical split (which is not the default for `:<nick>`).

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: Ah, I see. If other commands behave like that, that would be a reasonable thing, yes.

(But are you sure `:Explore` behaves like that? I only ever get a full-size buffer...)

We _don't_ want to recreate the zoo of `{L,H,S,V}Explore[!]` commands.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Okay, away from Explore since that does not have much to do with it, but rather the `:` command: `:25new`: `:5new`: It would make sense to me that if `:InspectTree` supports mods in front of it, that it would also support these counts, just like `:` and `:`, but also like other commands that open windows like `:Lexplore` and `:Sexplore` (the explore commands that open splits) It gives the user an easy way to control the width of the treesitter view

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Supporting a count modifier to specify window size is a good idea so long as it's not too complex to implement (I don't believe it should be).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> My point:
> 
> 1. `:10vnew InspectTree` -> supported
> 2. `:10InspectTree` -> no need to support

But `:10vnew` is not a modifier, so that won't work (it creates a 10-width split with a file named 'InspectTree'), and modifiers can't take a range/count, so `:10vertical InspecTree` is also not possible. If you want to give a range/count, you have to do it like this: `:<nick> 10InspectTree`

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: (shows how often I use these features...)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I think this works like one would expect, while respecting the default value of `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()` (which _will_ be `:60vnew`) when no mod or count given.

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_user_command('MyInspectTree', function(cmd)
  if cmd.mods ~= '' or cmd.count ~= 0 then
    local count = cmd.count ~= 0 and cmd.count or ''
    local new = cmd.mods ~= '' and 'new' or 'vnew'

    vim.treesitter.inspect_tree({
      command = ('%s %s%s'):<nick>(cmd.mods, count, new)
    })
  else
    vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()
  end
end, { count = true, desc = 'Inspect treesitter language tree for buffer' })
```

- `:InspectTree` --> `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree()`
- `:10InspectTree` --> `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree({command = '10vnew'})`
- `:<nick> InspectTree` --> `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree({command = 'topleft new'})`
- `:<nick> 10InspectTree` --> `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree({command = 'topleft 10new'})`
- `:<nick> topleft InspectTree` --> `vim.treesitter.inspect_tree({command = 'vertical topleft new'})`

Notice how only providing a count still keeps **v**new, but providing a mod uses new (because then you can specify where the window will go using the mod). I think this implementation comes most close to what the user would expect to happen. Let me know what you think.
